doc.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25

chapter: Beale Street and the early Memphis scene
title: Learning the blues in the Raven Avenue red-light district
summary: Shade grew up in a red-light district on Raven Avenue where pianos played blues day and night, including Handy's tunes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: After you got going on guitar, how did you learn how to play the blues?
Well, I was raised up where it wasn't nothing but a red light district and that's all they played, blues and things like that. What neighborhood?

What neighborhood was this? That was on Raven Avenue, just between Beale and Lennon on Raven. Used to call it Haddon's Avenue long years back. Used to be a gang of sporting people hanging around there and piano would be running night and day playing all kind of blues, Handys blues, St. Louis blues, Memphis blues, Yellow Dog, all city blues like that was out there, all battle house music.
